title: Topic 5 – KPIs and financial communication
source: Zusammenfassung von „IFRS Topic 5 fall 2026 student version“

blocks.text: Financial KPIs are based on accounting numbers but often not defined by the standards. They address performance (absolute profit, profit relative to capital), solvency (medium/long-term ability to repay debt) and liquidity (short-term). ESMA guidelines on alternative performance measures are an enforcement priority.

KPIs allow comparisons with peers and industry averages – but check that accounting policies (FIFO vs WAC, depreciation), estimates (useful lives, residual values – e.g. Lufthansa vs Ryanair), investment decisions and KPI definitions are comparable.

IFRS 18 (from 2027) adds defined subtotals and requires disclosures for management-defined performance measures: reconciliation to IFRS subtotals, explanation of purpose and calculation, explanation of changes.
Absolute performance numbers: gross margin, EBITDA, (recurring) operating profit, EBIT, EBT, net income. Only some are GAAP; EBITDA, recurring operating income etc. are non-GAAP.

EBITDA = operating profit + depreciation and amortisation. It differs from operating cash flow by working capital changes and income tax paid; it is used in valuation and debt covenants (net debt/EBITDA, EBITDA/interest). EBITDAaL deducts lease payments.
ROCE = EBIT × (1 − t) / capital employed; capital employed = net non-current assets + working capital needs = equity + net financial debt. DuPont: ROCE = NOPAT margin × capital employed turnover.
Other ratios: ROE = net income / equity, ROA = EBIT / total assets, ROI = EBIT / investment.
EVA = NOPAT − WACC × capital employed = (ROCE − WACC) × capital employed: value is created only if ROCE exceeds the cost of capital.
Free cash flow to the firm = operating cash flow − net capex (or EBIT(1 − t) + D&A − capex − increase in WCN). FCF to equity = FCFF + net increase in financial debt − financial expenses × (1 − t).
The capital necessary for the company to operate: net non-current assets + working capital needs, or equity + net financial debt.
Net operating profit after tax = EBIT × (1 − tax rate).
NOPAT minus a charge for the cost of capital employed (WACC × capital employed).

blocks.term: Free cash flow to the firm
blocks.text: Net cash generated by operations after the investments required to maintain productive capacity; available to all capital providers.
A performance measure not defined by the applicable accounting standards (e.g. EBITDA, ROCE, FCF).
